dedupe_keys.name: sniim mexico daily wholesale market prices and volumes of produce entering central markets by product state of origin and destination market

description: SNIIM, Mexico's national market information system, reports every working day the prices of food at the country's wholesale markets and how much produce enters the main central markets, and from where. It is run by the Ministry of Economy. The volumes of entry query gives, for about 110 fruit and vegetable products, the quantities arriving at five central markets, including the Central de Abasto of Iztapalapa in Mexico City and the markets of Guadalajara, Ecatepec, San Nicolás de los Garza (Nuevo León) and Mérida, split by state of origin and imports. Price pages cover fruit and vegetables, flowers, basic grains, sugar, edible oils, agricultural inputs, livestock, poultry and eggs, and fish at La Nueva Viga market, with daily and historical series. The data are free and available as query results on the web; no bulk download file or API was found on the pages read. Caveats: results are served page by page from forms, the start date of each series varies, and volumes cover only the five central markets listed. Simulation uses: building origin-destination food flow matrices into Mexico's largest cities, testing the effect of losing a producing state or highway corridor, and tracking supply shocks through wholesale prices. Related records: the Istanbul wholesale market flows (data-ibb-istanbul-wholesale-market-flows) are a comparable city market source, and the FAOSTAT food balances (data-faostat) give national supply.
